newsitem.title: GERMANY: German ProSieben seen ambitious on offer price.
newsitem.headline: German ProSieben seen ambitious on offer price.

text.p: ProSieben, Germany's first television broadcaster to seek a public listing for its shares, is likely to set an ambitious bookbuilding range when it gives details of its offering next week, analysts said on Friday.

The strong relative performance of comparable European media stocks in recent weeks, coupled with hopes for a high degree of retail investor interest, will encourage the firm to target issue proceeds of close to 1.4 billion marks, they said.
Analysts expect ProSieben on Monday to announce a range that could stretch from 62 marks to 80 marks for the 17.5 million preference non-voting shares that will make their market debut on July 7.

Pierre Drach, head of Frankfurt-based equity analysis group Independent Research and previously one of more bearish assessors of the stock, said that an eventual listing price near the top of the range was now a realistic possibility.
"It's clear that its banks are looking at a price in the seventies. It will no longer be cheap but a price even at the top of that range is achievable," he said.
Drach noted that stocks such as France's TF1 and Britain's BSkyB had been outperforming their respective markets lately, though BSkyB had taken a hit in recent days.
"For ProSieben, this (outperformance)...means it could run at a decent premium to the market in price-earnings terms," he said.

ProSieben's core attraction is that it offers large investors a slice of the German media sector via a company that describes itself as the country's most profitable broadcaster. Small investor demand is also due to be strong.
Analysts praised the channel's closely targeted advertising campaign for the issue.
"It has presented itself very well indeed," said Drach.

The channel is expected to play down lingering concern over its reliance on Hollywood material, insisting that it has insulated itself from expected increases in film right costs by having already secured its output until the year 2000.

One potential hurdle is continued uncertainty over the company's future ordinary shareholding structure. Directly after the flotation it will be dominated by Thomas Kirch, a member of the Kirch media group which supplies much of the feature film material.
"There has been a lot of conflicting information on the ...structure and some concrete statements on that would be welcome," said one analyst who did not want to be named.
Kirch will receive 60 percent of the group's ordinary shares after the issue and there has been speculation that he will run that interest down to just above 50 percent directly afterwards.
Rewe, the German retail group that owns a substantial minority share, is also being eyed closely for indications it might put its stake up for grabs in the medium-term, analysts added.
